arxiv-2102-08786.title: Walking Out of the Weisfeiler Leman Hierarchy: Graph Learning Beyond Message Passing
arxiv-2102-08786.creator: Jan Toenshoff toenshoff@informatik.rwth-aachen.de, Martin Ritzert ritzert@informatik.rwth-aachen.de, Hinrikus Wolf hinrikus@cs.rwth-aachen.de, Martin Grohe grohe@informatik.rwth-aachen.de
arxiv-2102-08786.description: Abstract We propose CRaWl , a novel neural network architecture for graph learning. Like graph neural networks, CRaWl layers update node features on a graph and thus can freely be combined or interleaved with GNN layers. Yet CRaWl operates fundamentally different from message passing graph neural networks.

arxiv-2102-13324.title: Spectroscopic Evidence on Realization of a Genuine Topological Nodal Line Semimetal in LaSbTe
arxiv-2102-13324.creator: Yang Wang 1,2♯ , Yuting Qian 1,2♯ , Meng Yang 1,2.3♯ , Hongxiang Chen 1,4♯ , Cong Li 1,2♯ , Zhiyun Tan 5 , Yongqing Cai 1,2 , Wenjuan Zhao 1,2 , Shunye Gao 1,2 , Ya Feng 6 , Shiv Kumar 7 , Eike F. Schwier 7,8 , Lin Zhao 1 , Hongming Weng 1,2,9,10 , Youguo Shi 1,2,3 , Gang Wang 1,2,9 , Youting Song 1
arxiv-2102-13324.description: Abstract The nodal line semimetals have attracted much attention due to their unique topological electronic structure and exotic physical properties. A genuine nodal line semimetal is qualified by the presence of Dirac nodes along a line in the momentum space that are protected against the spin-orbit coupling.

arxiv-2404-16957.title: Attributing Responsibility in AI-Induced Incidents: A Computational Reflective Equilibrium Framework for Accountability
arxiv-2404-16957.creator: Yunfei Ge Ya-Ting Yang, Quanyan Zhu
arxiv-2404-16957.description: Abstract The pervasive integration of Artificial Intelligence (AI) has introduced complex challenges in the responsibility and accountability in the event of incidents involving AI-enabled systems. The interconnectivity of these systems, ethical concerns of AI-induced incidents, coupled with uncertainties in AI technology and the absence of corresponding regulations, have made traditional responsibility attribution challenging.

arxiv-2410-21750.title: Learning and Unlearning of Fabricated Knowledge in Language Models
arxiv-2410-21750.creator: Chen Sun, Nolan Miller, Andrey Zhmoginov, Max Vladymyrov, Mark Sandler
arxiv-2410-21750.description: Abstract . What happens when a new piece of knowledge is introduced into the training data and how long does it last while a large language model (LM) continues to train? We investigate this question by injecting facts into LMs from a new probing dataset, “Outlandish”, which is designed to permit the testing of a spectrum of different fact types.

arxiv-2411-10948.title: Towards Accurate and Efficient Sub-8-Bit Integer Training
arxiv-2411-10948.creator: Wenjin Guo*, Donglai Liu*, Weiying Xie, Yunsong Li, Zihan Meng, Xuefei Ning, Shulin Zeng, Yu Wang, Jie Lei, Zhenman Fang
arxiv-2411-10948.description: Abstract Neural network training is a memory- and compute-intensive task. Quantization, which enables low-bitwidth formats in training, can significantly mitigate the workload. To reduce quantization error, recent methods have developed new data formats and additional pre-processing operations on quantizers. However, it remains quite challenging to achieve high accuracy and efficiency simultaneously.

arxiv-2507-08848.title: Assuring the Safety of Reinforcement Learning Components: AMLAS-RL
arxiv-2507-08848.creator: Calum Corrie Imrie 1 , Ioannis Stefanakos 1 , Sepeedeh Shahbeigi 1 , Richard Hawkins 1 , and Simon Burton 1
arxiv-2507-08848.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Calum Corrie Imrie 1 , Ioannis Stefanakos 1 , Sepeedeh Shahbeigi 1 , Richard Hawkins 1 , and Simon Burton 1. The rapid advancement of machine learning (ML) has led to its increasing integration into cyber-physical systems (CPS) across diverse domains. While CPS offer powerful capabilities, incorporating ML components introduces significant safety and assurance challenges.

arxiv-2601-04377.title: Disco-RAG: Discourse-Aware Retrieval-Augmented Generation
arxiv-2601-04377.creator: Dongqi Liu, Hang Ding, Qiming Feng, Jian Li, Xurong Xie, Zhucun Xue, Chengjie Wang, Jiangning Zhang, Yabiao Wang
arxiv-2601-04377.description: Abstract Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) has emerged as an important means of enhancing the performance of large language models (LLMs) in knowledge-intensive tasks. However, most existing RAG strategies treat retrieved passages in a flat and unstructured way, which prevents the model from capturing structural cues and constrains its ability to synthesize knowledge from dispersed evidence across documents.

pmc-10647092.creator: JinBo Chen, Yang Wang, LongBin Yu, Weina Ren, Yan Sheng
pmc-10647092.description: BackgroundAnterior scleral staphyloma is a relatively rare disease characterized by thinning and expansion of sclera. pmc-11345834.title: Bidirectional Energy Flow in the Photosystem II Supercomplex
pmc-11345834.creator: Cristina Leonardo, Shiun-Jr Yang, Kaydren Orcutt, Masakazu Iwai, Eric A Arsenault, Graham R Fleming
pmc-11345834.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). The water-splitting capability of Photosystem II (PSII) of plants and green algae requires the system to balance efficient light harvesting along with effective photoprotection against excitation in excess of the photosynthetic capacity, particularly under the naturally fluctuating sunlight intensity. The comparatively flat energy landscape of the multicomponent structure, inferred from the spectra of the individual pigment–protein complexes and the rather narrow and featureless absorption spectrum, is well known.

pmc-12827429.creator: Ye Jin, Jing He, Dongmei Fan, Lu Wang, Ning Cui, Yangyang Liu, Da Liu
pmc-12827429.description: The human gut microbiota serves as a critical hub for host metabolic and immune regulation. Disruption of its homeostasis is closely associated with diseases such as Inflammatory Bowel Disease (IBD), metabolic syndrome, and colorectal cancer. Modern dietary and environmental factors are known to exacerbate this dysbiosis, highlighting the need for innovative interventions capable of modulating the gut ecosystem.

pmc-13562910.title: Extent of Endobronchial Ultrasound Nodal Sampling and Risk of Pathologic N2 Upstaging in Clinical N0–N1 Non‐Small Cell Lung Cancer
pmc-13562910.creator: Min Jee Kim, Jae Cheol Lee, Chang‐Min Choi, Sei Won Lee, Jae Seung Lee, Kyung‐Wook Jo, Ho Cheol Kim, Jee Hwan Ahn, Jang Ho Lee, Dong‐Gon Hyun, Wonjun Ji
pmc-13562910.description: BackgroundEndobronchial ultrasound (EBUS)–guided transbronchial needle aspiration (TBNA) is strongly recommended for mediastinal staging in resectable non–small cell lung cancer (NSCLC). However, the optimal sampling extent remains uncertain. This study aimed to evaluate whether the extent of nodal sampling during staging EBUS is associated with pathologic N2 upstaging in clinical N0–N1 NSCLC.

pmc-13593600.title: Investigation of the estrous status in Thoroughbred mares coming to a stud farm for breeding
pmc-13593600.creator: Yuko TOISHI, Nobuo TSUNODA
pmc-13593600.description: In the Thoroughbred industry, artificial insemination is prohibited. Veterinarians examine mares to determine the time to breed; however, some mares refuse breeding at the stud farm. Estrous status was investigated at breeding in 12,388 mares by measuring blood progesterone (P4) concentrations, and conception rates between mares in estrus and in the luteal phase were compared.
